<Lam 1:1a> How the city sits solitary
 - There are all kinds of laments in the Bible. The Song of the Bow is one of them too. But in all of human history there has never been, before or since, a lament as heartbreaking as this. Jeremiah said goodbye to those people in Egypt, came back, and walked one last time through the streets of Jerusalem, where for 40 years he had preached the word with tears of blood and prayed. And the panorama that unfolded before his eyes was truly horrific.
 1) Jerusalem fell, and Solomon's holy temple burned and collapsed
 2) The royal family, the nobles and the great men were killed or taken captive
 3) The little children who used to play in the streets were killed by the enemy or taken captive
 4) In the streets the slaughterers' swords were still running wild, and in house after house the stench of rotting bodies no one could clear away was so bad you couldn't lift your eyes or your nose

5) The women of Jerusalem took the children that came out from between their own legs, the children they had raised in their own hands, and were eating their flesh
 6) Skin that had been ruddy like coral and smooth like polished sapphire dried up like sticks from the fever of hunger and turned black as an oven, so no one in the streets could recognize them
 7) Even when the feasts and festivals came, no one came and went in the streets of Jerusalem
 8) The city that was once like a princess had now become pitiful
 9) Little children begged for bread but no one broke it for them; Zion spread out her hands but there was no one to comfort her
 10) Even crying until her eyes were raw with tears, there was no one to comfort her
 11) Boys and girls, young men and women were killed before they could even bloom
 16) The enemies violated the women in every city and moved on
 17) Treasures and vessels kept for generations were all plundered
 18) Things like joy, faith, hope and love in people's hearts were all completely destroyed.
